literal: Begging when thinking of, the mind will melt; withholding when thinking of, even that which exists, without, will perish.
translation: The mind melts at the mere thought of begging; but at the thought of the refusal to give, even that which exists will perish and be utterly lost.
modern: இரந்து கேட்பதை நினைத்தாலே மனம் உருகும்; ஆனால், கொடுப்பதற்கு மனம் இல்லாமல் மறைத்து வைப்பதை நினைத்தால், உள்ளதும் இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the pain of begging with the deeper misery of hoarding and refusing to give. The poet says that the mere thought of having to beg for sustenance makes one's heart melt with sorrow. However, when one thinks of those who hide their wealth and refuse to give (karavu), even the existing dignity, lineage, or wealth of the hoarder is completely destroyed. The word 'karavu' refers to the act of concealing one's resources to avoid giving, and 'uḷḷatūum' emphasizes that even the basic existence or possessions of such a person will perish.
